google_compute_beta_network_endpoint_gro: `google_compute_beta_network_endpoint_group` groups real backend endpoints a load balancer can route to -- individual VM IP:port pairs, serverless services, or endpoints outside Google Cloud -- a more granular real target than pointing a load balancer at a whole instance group.

google_compute_beta_region_composite_hea: `google_compute_beta_region_composite_health_check` combines the real health states of multiple individual health sources into one overall health verdict for a regional published service -- the service counts as healthy only when enough of its own real health sources agree it is.
google_compute_beta_region_disk: `google_compute_beta_region_disk` is a persistent disk replicated synchronously across two zones in a region, rather than living in just one zone -- real protection against a single zone failure, at the cost of the extra real replication overhead.

google_compute_beta_region_health_check: `google_compute_beta_region_health_check` is the regional counterpart to a global health check, used by regional load balancers and regional managed instance groups to determine real backend health within that one region.

google_compute_network_edge_security_ser: `google_compute_network_edge_security_service` enables advanced network DDoS protection for every applicable regional resource -- network load balancers, protocol forwarding, VMs with public IPs -- in one region at once, by attaching a Cloud Armor network security policy to it.
google_compute_network_endpoint_group: `google_compute_network_endpoint_group` groups real backend endpoints a load balancer can route to -- individual VM IP:port pairs, serverless services, or endpoints outside Google Cloud -- a more granular real target than pointing a load balancer at a whole instance group.
google_compute_network_firewall_policy: `google_compute_network_firewall_policy` is a global, real, reusable set of firewall rules attachable to a VPC network -- the network-scoped counterpart to a hierarchical (organization/folder-level) firewall policy.
google_compute_node_group: `google_compute_node_group` is a real collection of sole-tenant nodes -- physical servers dedicated entirely to your own project -- that VMs can be placed onto for real, dedicated hardware isolation.
google_compute_node_template: `google_compute_node_template` defines the real hardware specification -- node type, CPU overcommit settings -- that a sole-tenant node group uses to actually provision the physical nodes inside it.
google_compute_organization_security_pol: `google_compute_organization_security_policy` is a real, hierarchical firewall policy enforceable across an entire organization or folder -- rules set here can't be overridden by a lower-level policy, giving organization-wide admins one real place to manage critical, non-negotiable firewall rules.
google_compute_packet_mirroring: `google_compute_packet_mirroring` clones real network traffic to and from a set of instances and sends the copy to a collector, without disrupting the original traffic at all -- used for real, out-of-band security monitoring and intrusion detection.
google_compute_public_advertised_prefix: `google_compute_public_advertised_prefix` registers a real, top-level block of your own public IP addresses with Google, the first real step before any smaller delegated prefix carved out of it can be used on Google Cloud.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefix: `google_compute_public_delegated_prefix` carves a real, smaller, regional block of addresses out of an already-registered public advertised prefix, delegating that specific slice for actual use within one region.
google_compute_region_autoscaler: `google_compute_region_autoscaler` is the regional counterpart to a zonal autoscaler -- automatically resizing a regional managed instance group (one spread across multiple zones in a region) based on the same real load signals.
google_compute_region_backend_bucket: `google_compute_region_backend_bucket` is the regional counterpart to a global backend bucket, letting a regional load balancer serve content directly from Cloud Storage.
google_compute_region_backend_service: `google_compute_region_backend_service` is the regional counterpart to a global backend service -- the same real health check, timeout, and traffic distribution configuration, scoped to backends within one region for a regional load balancer.
google_compute_region_commitment: `google_compute_region_commitment` is a regional committed-use discount -- a real, one- or three-year commitment to a specific amount of vCPU, memory, or GPU usage in one region, in exchange for a lower real hourly rate than on-demand pricing.
google_compute_region_composite_health_c: `google_compute_region_composite_health_check` combines the real health states of multiple individual health sources into one overall health verdict for a regional published service -- the service counts as healthy only when enough of its own real health sources agree it is.
google_compute_region_disk: `google_compute_region_disk` is a persistent disk replicated synchronously across two zones in a region, rather than living in just one zone -- real protection against a single zone failure, at the cost of the extra real replication overhead.
google_compute_region_health_aggregation: `google_compute_region_health_aggregation_policy` defines the real conditions -- a minimum percentage of healthy backends, a minimum count -- that a composite health check actually applies when deciding whether a regional published service as a whole should be considered healthy.
google_compute_region_health_check: `google_compute_region_health_check` is the regional counterpart to a global health check, used by regional load balancers and regional managed instance groups to determine real backend health within that one region.
google_compute_region_health_check_servi: `google_compute_region_health_check_service` is the regional configuration tying a health check to the real notification endpoints that should be told when a monitored resource's own health status actually changes.
google_compute_region_health_source: `google_compute_region_health_source` is one real, individual input a composite health check combines with others -- a Private Service Connect endpoint's own health, for instance -- into that composite check's single, overall health verdict.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man: `google_compute_region_instance_group_manager` is the regional counterpart to a zonal instance group manager -- managing a managed instance group whose real instances are spread across multiple zones in one region for higher availability.

`google_compute_region_instance_group_manager_resize_request` is the regional counterpart to a zonal resize request -- requesting a real, specific number of instances be added at once to a regional managed instance group.
google_compute_region_instance_template: `google_compute_region_instance_template` is the regional counterpart to a global instance template, usable specifically by regional managed instance groups.
google_compute_region_instant_snapshot: `google_compute_region_instant_snapshot` is the regional counterpart to a zonal instant snapshot -- a fast, point-in-time copy of a regional (multi-zone replicated) persistent disk.
google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_g: `google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_group` is the regional counterpart to a zonal instant snapshot group, capturing a consistent, real snapshot across multiple regional disks at once.
google_compute_region_network_endpoint_g: `google_compute_region_network_endpoint_group` is the regional counterpart to a global network endpoint group -- grouping real backend endpoints within one region for a regional load balancer to route to, including serverless (Cloud Run, App Engine) backends specifically.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p: `google_compute_region_network_firewall_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global network firewall policy -- a real, reusable rule set attachable to networks, scoped to a single region.
google_compute_region_notification_endpo: `google_compute_region_notification_endpoint` is the regional counterpart to a global notification endpoint -- receiving real status-change notifications from a regional health check service the moment a monitored resource's own health changes.
google_compute_region_security_policy: `google_compute_region_security_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global Cloud Armor security policy, applied to backends behind a regional, rather than global, load balancer.
google_compute_region_snapshot: `google_compute_region_snapshot` is the regional counterpart to a standard, multi-region snapshot -- a real, durable, point-in-time disk backup stored specifically within one region rather than replicated more broadly.
google_compute_region_ssl_certificate: `google_compute_region_ssl_certificate` is the regional counterpart to a global SSL certificate, usable by a regional HTTPS or SSL proxy load balancer to actually terminate TLS.
google_compute_region_ssl_policy: `google_compute_region_ssl_policy` is the regional counterpart to a global SSL policy, controlling which real TLS versions and cipher suites a regional load balancer accepts.
google_compute_region_target_http_proxy: `google_compute_region_target_http_proxy` is the regional counterpart to a global target HTTP proxy -- routing real, unencrypted HTTP traffic to a backend service via a regional URL map.
google_compute_region_target_https_proxy: `google_compute_region_target_https_proxy` is the regional counterpart to a global target HTTPS proxy, terminating real TLS and routing traffic to a backend service via a regional URL map.
google_compute_region_target_tcp_proxy: `google_compute_region_target_tcp_proxy` is the regional counterpart to a global target TCP proxy, routing real TCP traffic to a backend service scoped to one region.
google_compute_region_url_map: `google_compute_region_url_map` is the regional counterpart to a global URL map -- the real, host- and path-based routing rules a regional HTTP(S) load balancer uses to decide which backend service handles a given request.
google_compute_reservation: `google_compute_reservation` sets aside real compute capacity -- a specific machine type and count, in a specific zone -- guaranteeing it's actually available for your own VMs to consume, rather than competing for capacity with every other customer at boot time.
google_compute_resource_policy: `google_compute_resource_policy` is a real, reusable schedule attachable to disks or instances -- automated snapshot creation, or a real start/stop schedule for an instance -- defined once and applied to many resources rather than scripted separately for each.
google_compute_rollout_plan: `google_compute_rollout_plan` defines the real waves a change should roll out in -- grouped by zone or region, with a configurable delay between each wave -- used by global VM extension policies to apply a change gradually across a fleet instead of everywhere at once.
google_compute_route: `google_compute_route` tells a VPC network's own routing table where to actually send traffic matching a specific real destination IP range -- to a gateway, an instance, or another real next hop.
google_compute_router: `google_compute_router` runs real, dynamic BGP routing for a VPC network -- exchanging routes with an on-premises network over Cloud VPN or Interconnect rather than relying on static routes alone.
google_compute_security_policy: `google_compute_security_policy` is a Cloud Armor policy -- real WAF rules, rate limiting, and DDoS protection -- attached to a backend service to filter traffic before it ever reaches a real backend.
google_compute_service_attachment: `google_compute_service_attachment` publishes a real service through Private Service Connect, letting other VPC networks (including ones outside your own organization) connect to it privately without that traffic ever traversing the public internet.
google_compute_snapshot: `google_compute_snapshot` is a real, durable, incremental point-in-time backup of a persistent disk, storable and restorable across zones and regions -- the standard mechanism for real disk backup and disaster recovery.
google_compute_ssl_certificate: `google_compute_ssl_certificate` holds a real TLS certificate and private key a global HTTPS or SSL proxy load balancer uses to actually terminate encrypted connections.
google_compute_ssl_policy: `google_compute_ssl_policy` controls which real TLS versions and cipher suites a global load balancer accepts, letting you enforce a stricter real minimum than the platform default.
google_compute_storage_pool: `google_compute_storage_pool` is a real, shared pool of Hyperdisk capacity and performance that multiple individual disks draw from together, instead of each disk provisioning and paying for its own dedicated capacity separately.
google_compute_subnetwork: `google_compute_subnetwork` carves a real, regional range of IP addresses out of a VPC network -- the actual scope instances get their internal IP addresses from, and the resource region-specific settings like Private Google Access are configured on.
google_compute_target_grpc_proxy: `google_compute_target_grpc_proxy` routes real gRPC traffic to a backend service via a URL map, the gRPC-specific counterpart to a target HTTP proxy.
google_compute_target_http_proxy: `google_compute_target_http_proxy` routes real, unencrypted HTTP traffic to a backend service according to a global URL map's own rules.
google_compute_target_https_proxy: `google_compute_target_https_proxy` terminates real TLS and routes the decrypted traffic to a backend service according to a global URL map.
google_compute_target_instance: `google_compute_target_instance` designates a single real VM instance as the destination for a forwarding rule -- a real, simple target for traffic that doesn't need a full load balancer in front of it.
google_compute_target_pool: `google_compute_target_pool` is the legacy target for a network load balancer -- a real, simple group of instances traffic is distributed across, superseded for new deployments by backend services but still real, supported API surface.
google_compute_target_ssl_proxy: `google_compute_target_ssl_proxy` terminates real TLS for non-HTTP TCP traffic and forwards the decrypted stream to a backend service, the SSL-proxy counterpart to a target HTTPS proxy.
google_compute_target_tcp_proxy: `google_compute_target_tcp_proxy` proxies real TCP traffic straight through to a backend service without terminating TLS at all, for protocols that need to keep their own encryption intact end to end.
google_compute_target_vpn_gateway: `google_compute_target_vpn_gateway` is the legacy, Classic VPN gateway resource representing Google's own side of a VPN tunnel -- superseded by the newer HA VPN gateway for new deployments, but still real, supported API surface.
google_compute_url_map: `google_compute_url_map` defines the real, host- and path-based routing rules a global HTTP(S) load balancer uses to decide which backend service actually handles a given incoming request.
google_compute_vpn_gateway: `google_compute_vpn_gateway` represents the modern, HA VPN version of Google's own side of a VPN connection -- built for real 99.99% availability via redundant real interfaces, the replacement for the older Classic target VPN gateway.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel: `google_compute_vpn_tunnel` is one real, encrypted IPsec tunnel between a Google VPN gateway and an external peer -- the actual, active connection real traffic flows through once a VPN gateway is set up.
google_compute_wire_group: `google_compute_wire_group` configures real bandwidth and traffic settings on top of a Cross-Site Interconnect connection -- VLAN or port mode, unmetered bandwidth, optional MACsec encryption -- the resource that actually carries traffic across a cross-site network.
google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policy: `google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policy` is the zonal counterpart to a global VM extension policy -- declaring which extensions VM Extension Manager should install on matching VMs within one specific zone rather than across every zone and region at once.
google_config_deployment: `google_config_deployment` applies a Terraform configuration through Infrastructure Manager, Google Cloud's own managed Terraform execution service.
google_config_deployment_group: `google_config_deployment_group` groups related Infrastructure Manager deployments together, for coordinated multi-deployment operations like ordered updates.
google_config_preview: `google_config_preview` runs a dry-run (plan-only) evaluation of an Infrastructure Manager Terraform configuration, showing the change(s) it would make without actually applying them.
google_connectors_connection: `google_connectors_connection` is an Integration Connectors connection, a managed link to a third-party or Google Cloud system (e.g. Salesforce, BigQuery, a JDBC database) that other services like Application Integration and Apigee can invoke without hand-building the underlying API client.
google_connectors_custom_connector: `google_connectors_custom_connector` defines a custom Integration Connectors connector for a system with no built-in connector, built from an OpenAPI specification.
google_connectors_custom_connector_versi: `google_connectors_custom_connector_version` is one versioned revision of a custom connector's own OpenAPI specification and configuration.
google_connectors_end_user_authenticatio: `google_connectors_end_user_authentication` configures per-end-user OAuth credentials for a connection used in an end-user authentication (rather than a single shared service-account) flow.
google_connectors_endpoint_attachment: `google_connectors_endpoint_attachment` is a Private Service Connect endpoint Integration Connectors uses to privately reach a backend that isn't exposed to the public internet.
google_connectors_event_subscription: `google_connectors_event_subscription` subscribes a connection to real-time event notifications from its own backend system, delivered to a configured destination.
google_connectors_managed_zone: `google_connectors_managed_zone` is a private DNS zone Integration Connectors uses to resolve a backend's own hostname when connecting over a private network path.
google_contactcenteraiplatform_contact_c: `google_contactcenteraiplatform_contact_center` is a real, tenant-level Contact Center AI Platform (CCAI Platform) instance, a full-stack contact center for queuing and routing customer interactions across voice and digital channels, provisioned and managed at the project and location level.
google_contactcenterinsights_analyse: `google_contactcenterinsights_analyse` (an Analysis) runs Contact Center AI Insights' own ML-based processing over a single conversation, producing sentiment, entity, intent, and issue detection results.
google_contactcenterinsights_analysis_ru: `google_contactcenterinsights_analysis_rule` automatically triggers a Contact Center AI Insights analysis on conversation(s) matching a defined filter, instead of requiring each analysis to be requested manually.
google_contactcenterinsights_assessment: `google_contactcenterinsights_assessment` records a completed quality assurance evaluation of a conversation against a scorecard, holding the scored answer(s) to each of the scorecard's own question(s).

google_contactcenterinsights_assistant_s: `google_contactcenterinsights_assistant_session` is a single live session of Conversational Insights' own real-time Agent Assist, providing an active human agent with suggested response(s) and information while a conversation is in progress.
google_contactcenterinsights_authorized_: `google_contactcenterinsights_authorized_view` restricts a principal's own access within Contact Center AI Insights to a defined subset of conversation data, for role-based data isolation.

google_contactcenterinsights_auto_labeli: `google_contactcenterinsights_auto_labeling_rule` automatically assigns a feedback label to conversation(s) matching a defined condition, building a labeled dataset without manual tagging.
google_contactcenterinsights_chart: `google_contactcenterinsights_chart` defines a single visualization (e.g. a trend line or breakdown) displayed on a Contact Center AI Insights dashboard.
google_contactcenterinsights_conversatio: `google_contactcenterinsights_conversation` is a single imported customer interaction (a call transcript or chat log) that Contact Center AI Insights analyzes for sentiment, topics, and quality signals.
google_contactcenterinsights_dashboard: `google_contactcenterinsights_dashboard` is a saved collection of chart(s) presenting Contact Center AI Insights analytics, e.g. call volume or sentiment trends over time.
google_contactcenterinsights_dataset: `google_contactcenterinsights_dataset` is a named collection of conversation(s) grouped together in Contact Center AI Insights, e.g. for training an issue model or running a bulk analysis.
google_contactcenterinsights_feedback_la: `google_contactcenterinsights_feedback_label` records a human-assigned ground-truth label on a conversation, used to evaluate and improve Contact Center AI Insights' own model accuracy.
google_contactcenterinsights_issue: `google_contactcenterinsights_issue` is a single, automatically discovered topic or theme (e.g. `billing dispute`) within a Contact Center AI Insights issue model, that conversations are classified against.
google_contactcenterinsights_issue_model: `google_contactcenterinsights_issue_model` trains an ML model over a set of conversations to automatically discover and classify the recurring issue(s) customers are calling about.
google_contactcenterinsights_phrase_matc: `google_contactcenterinsights_phrase_matcher` defines a rule matching specific phrase(s) or pattern(s) spoken during a conversation, flagging matching conversations for Contact Center AI Insights' own analysis.
google_contactcenterinsights_qa_question: `google_contactcenterinsights_qa_question` defines a single quality-assurance question (e.g. `Did the agent greet the customer?`) within a QA scorecard, either scored manually or automatically.

google_contactcenterinsights_revision: `google_contactcenterinsights_revision` is a saved, versioned snapshot of a QA scorecard's own question set, letting past assessments remain tied to the exact scorecard version they were scored against.
google_contactcenterinsights_view: `google_contactcenterinsights_view` defines a saved, reusable filter over Contact Center AI Insights conversation data, used to scope dashboards, exports, or bulk analysis to a specific subset.

google_dataplex_aspect_type: `google_dataplex_aspect_type` defines a reusable, structured schema for a business or technical metadata facet (e.g. a data quality score or a PII classification) that can be attached to any Dataplex catalog entry as an aspect.
google_dataplex_asset: `google_dataplex_asset` registers an underlying data source -- a Cloud Storage bucket or BigQuery dataset -- with a Dataplex zone, bringing it under that zone's own governance and discovery.
google_dataplex_attribute: `google_dataplex_attribute` defines a single node in a Dataplex data taxonomy's own classification hierarchy, e.g. a sensitivity level like `Confidential`.
google_dataplex_binding: `google_dataplex_binding` grants IAM role(s) to principal(s) scoped to a specific set of resources within Dataplex Universal Catalog (rebranded Knowledge Catalog as of April 2026), narrower than a project-level IAM binding.
google_dataplex_category: `google_dataplex_category` defines a data classification node within a Dataplex policy tag taxonomy, used to enforce BigQuery column-level access control based on sensitivity.
google_dataplex_data_asset: `google_dataplex_data_asset` is a curated data asset packaged as part of a Dataplex Data Product -- one of the underlying dataset(s), table(s), or view(s) that make up a governed, business-ready data offering.
google_dataplex_data_attribute_binding: `google_dataplex_data_attribute_binding` attaches a data taxonomy attribute (e.g. a sensitivity classification) to a specific data asset, resource, or column within Dataplex.
google_dataplex_data_domain: `google_dataplex_data_domain` groups related data product(s) and their own governance ownership under a single business domain (e.g. `Finance` or `Marketing`) within Dataplex's data mesh model.
google_dataplex_data_product: `google_dataplex_data_product` is a curated, business-ready package of data asset(s), documentation, quality contracts, and governance controls assembled in Dataplex to solve a specific business problem, the unit Dataplex's data mesh capability is organized around.

google_dataplex_encryption_config: `google_dataplex_encryption_config` configures a customer-managed encryption key for Dataplex to use when encrypting a lake's own managed resources.
google_dataplex_entity: `google_dataplex_entity` registers a single structured or semi-structured data entity (a table-like object backed by files or a BigQuery table) discovered or defined within a Dataplex zone.
google_dataplex_entry: `google_dataplex_entry` is a single cataloged item in Dataplex Universal Catalog (Knowledge Catalog) -- a table, file set, dashboard, or any other real or logical asset -- carrying its own metadata and aspect(s).

google_dataplex_entry_link: `google_dataplex_entry_link` defines a typed relationship between two Dataplex catalog entries, e.g. connecting a business glossary term to the specific table column it defines.
google_dataplex_entry_type: `google_dataplex_entry_type` defines the schema (which aspect types are required or allowed) that catalog entries of a given kind must conform to in Dataplex Universal Catalog.
google_dataplex_glossary: `google_dataplex_glossary` is a business glossary in Dataplex Universal Catalog -- a hierarchical structure of business term(s) and category/categories that can be linked to real catalog entries for shared, governed terminology.
google_dataplex_lake: `google_dataplex_lake` is the top-level organizational container in Dataplex, grouping related zone(s) and their own underlying data assets under one logical data lake.
google_dataplex_metadata_feed: `google_dataplex_metadata_feed` triggers automatic Dataplex Catalog entry updates whenever a linked resource's own metadata (e.g. a BigQuery table's schema) changes.

google_dataplex_term: `google_dataplex_term` is a single business term defined within a Dataplex Universal Catalog glossary, e.g. a shared definition of `Customer Lifetime Value`.
google_dataplex_zone: `google_dataplex_zone` subdivides a Dataplex lake into a raw or curated area, each with its own data-management policy, that asset(s) are attached to.

google_dataproc_batch: `google_dataproc_batch` runs a single Spark, PySpark, or SparkR workload on serverless Dataproc, without the caller having to provision or manage a persistent cluster.

google_dataproc_node_group: `google_dataproc_node_group` defines a named group of additional worker node(s) within a Dataproc cluster, e.g. a set of preemptible/Spot nodes distinct from the cluster's own primary workers.
google_dataproc_session: `google_dataproc_session` is an interactive, serverless Spark session on Dataproc, letting a notebook or client run multiple Spark statements against shared, live compute without a persistent cluster.
google_dataproc_session_template: `google_dataproc_session_template` defines a reusable configuration (runtime version, resource sizing) new Dataproc interactive sessions can be created from.
google_dataproc_workflow_template: `google_dataproc_workflow_template` defines a reusable, ordered graph of Dataproc job(s) (with dependencies between them) that can be instantiated and run as a single managed workflow.

google_iam_key: `google_iam_key` is a cryptographic key belonging to a service account, a Workforce Identity Federation provider, or a Workload Identity Federation provider, depending on which resource it's attached to.

google_iam_provider: `google_iam_provider` configures how an external identity provider (e.g. a corporate SSO system or a CI/CD platform's own OIDC issuer) is trusted within a Workforce or Workload Identity Federation pool.
google_iam_role: `google_iam_role` is a custom IAM role, a named, project- or organization-scoped bundle of permissions defined when none of Google Cloud's own predefined roles fit exactly.
google_iam_scim_tenant: `google_iam_scim_tenant` configures SCIM-based automatic user and group provisioning for a Workforce Identity Federation pool provider, syncing identities from an external directory.
google_iam_service_account: `google_iam_service_account` is a Google Cloud service account, a non-human identity applications and workloads authenticate as to call Google Cloud APIs.
google_iam_token: `google_iam_token` represents a short-lived OAuth access token generated on demand for a service account via impersonation, the real, callable output of the IAM Service Account Credentials API's own `generateAccessToken` method.
google_iam_v2beta_policy: `google_iam_v2beta_policy` is a real IAM v2 policy resource -- its own kind and rules -- a newer, more general policy shape than the classic Cloud IAM binding list, so access rules can be expressed and attached the same way regardless of which real IAM v2 policy kind they belong to.
google_iam_workforce_pool: `google_iam_workforce_pool` is a Workforce Identity Federation pool, letting an organization's own external workforce (e.g. employees federated through a corporate identity provider) access Google Cloud without a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity account.
google_iam_workload_identity_pool: `google_iam_workload_identity_pool` is a Workload Identity Federation pool, letting a workload running outside Google Cloud (e.g. in another cloud, or on-premises) authenticate using its own external credentials instead of a downloaded service account key.
google_iampolicies_iam_policy: `google_iampolicies_iam_policy` is a real, generic IAM v2 Policy resource, used to define Deny Policies and Principal Access Boundary Policies at organization, folder, or project scope -- Google Cloud's own newer, `kind`-discriminated policy model, distinct from the classic IAM allow-policy bindings on individual resources.
google_iap_brand: `google_iap_brand` configures the OAuth consent screen branding (app name, support email) shown to users authenticating through Identity-Aware Proxy for a project.
google_iap_dest_group: `google_iap_dest_group` defines a named group of TCP destination(s) that Identity-Aware Proxy's own TCP forwarding tunnel access can be scoped to.
google_iap_identity_aware_proxy_client: `google_iap_identity_aware_proxy_client` is an additional OAuth client registered under an Identity-Aware Proxy brand, letting more than one client application authenticate through the same IAP-protected resource.

google_identitytoolkit_inbound_saml_conf: `google_identitytoolkit_inbound_saml_config` configures a SAML-based enterprise identity provider Identity Platform accepts sign-ins from.

google_logging_bucket: `google_logging_bucket` is a Cloud Logging log bucket, the storage container ingested log entries are retained in for a configured retention period and made queryable from.
google_logging_exclusion: `google_logging_exclusion` filters out matching log entries before they're ingested into a Cloud Logging sink or bucket, reducing storage cost and noise for logs that don't need to be kept.
google_logging_link: `google_logging_link` links a Cloud Logging log bucket to a BigQuery dataset, enabling that bucket's own log data to be queried directly with SQL via BigQuery's own analytics engine.
google_logging_log_scope: `google_logging_log_scope` defines a named set of log bucket(s) or resource(s) that a Cloud Logging query can be scoped to search across together.

google_logging_sink: `google_logging_sink` routes matching Cloud Logging log entries to an external destination (a Cloud Storage bucket, BigQuery dataset, or Pub/Sub topic) for export outside the default logging retention.

google_policysimulator_replay: `google_policysimulator_replay` is a Policy Simulator replay, re-evaluating real past IAM access attempts under both a resource's current policy and a proposed policy change, then comparing the two results to show exactly how a member's access would change if the proposed policy were applied.

google_privateca_ca_pool: `google_privateca_ca_pool` groups related Certificate Authority Service certificate authorities together, sharing issuance policy and letting certificates be requested from the pool without pinning to one specific CA.
google_privateca_certificate: `google_privateca_certificate` is an X.509 certificate issued by a Certificate Authority Service CA, either directly requested or generated from a Certificate Manager Google-managed certificate.
google_privateca_certificate_authority: `google_privateca_certificate_authority` is a private Certificate Authority managed by Certificate Authority Service, issuing X.509 certificate(s) within its own CA pool.
google_privateca_certificate_template: `google_privateca_certificate_template` constrains and pre-fills the fields a Certificate Authority Service CA is permitted to issue certificates with, enforcing organizational certificate policy.
google_privilegedaccessmanager_entitleme: `google_privilegedaccessmanager_entitlement` defines a role or permission grant that eligible principal(s) can request temporary, approval-gated access to through Privileged Access Manager, instead of holding it permanently.
google_privilegedaccessmanager_grant: `google_privilegedaccessmanager_grant` is a single, time-bound activation of a Privileged Access Manager entitlement, giving a principal the underlying access for a limited window after approval.
google_pubsub_schema: `google_pubsub_schema` defines the Avro or Protocol Buffer message schema a Pub/Sub topic's own published messages are validated against.
google_pubsub_snapshot: `google_pubsub_snapshot` captures a Pub/Sub subscription's own acknowledgment state at a point in time, letting the subscription be seeked back to it later to replay messages.
google_pubsub_subscription: `google_pubsub_subscription` attaches to a Pub/Sub topic and delivers its own published messages to a consumer, either by pull or push, tracking per-message acknowledgment.
google_pubsub_topic: `google_pubsub_topic` is a Pub/Sub topic, the named resource publishers send message(s) to and subscription(s) receive message(s) from.
google_pubsub_v1beta1a_subscription: `google_pubsub_v1beta1a_subscription` attaches to a Pub/Sub topic and delivers its own published messages to a consumer, either by pull or push, tracking per-message acknowledgment.
google_pubsub_v1beta1a_topic: `google_pubsub_v1beta1a_topic` is a Pub/Sub topic, the named resource publishers send message(s) to and subscription(s) receive message(s) from.
google_pubsub_v1beta2_subscription: `google_pubsub_v1beta2_subscription` attaches to a Pub/Sub topic and delivers its own published messages to a consumer, either by pull or push, tracking per-message acknowledgment.
google_pubsub_v1beta2_topic: `google_pubsub_v1beta2_topic` is a Pub/Sub topic, the named resource publishers send message(s) to and subscription(s) receive message(s) from.
google_pubsublite_reservation: `google_pubsublite_reservation` purchases a fixed pool of Pub/Sub Lite throughput capacity that topic(s) draw from, for predictable, capacity-based pricing.
google_pubsublite_subscription: `google_pubsublite_subscription` attaches to a Pub/Sub Lite topic and delivers its own published messages to a consumer, tracking read position per partition.
google_pubsublite_topic: `google_pubsublite_topic` is a Pub/Sub Lite topic, a lower-cost, zonal alternative to standard Pub/Sub with partitioned, capacity-based throughput.
google_rapidmigrationassessment_annotati: `google_rapidmigrationassessment_annotation` records real, user-supplied context (such as intent or priority) against assets discovered by a Rapid Migration Assessment `google_rapidmigrationassessment_collector`, informing Google's own first-party migration assessment and planning output.
google_rapidmigrationassessment_collecto: `google_rapidmigrationassessment_collector` is a real Rapid Migration Assessment collector, the agent deployed into an existing environment to discover and inventory the real servers, workloads, and dependencies a migration-planning assessment needs.
google_recaptchaenterprise_firewallpolic: `google_recaptchaenterprise_firewallpolicy` defines a rule reCAPTCHA Enterprise's WAF integration applies to matching request(s), e.g. blocking traffic below a risk-score threshold.
google_recaptchaenterprise_key: `google_recaptchaenterprise_key` registers a site or app with reCAPTCHA Enterprise, the credential used to request and validate risk assessment(s) for its own traffic.
google_redis_acl_policy: `google_redis_acl_policy` defines Redis ACL rule(s) (which command(s) and key pattern(s) a user is permitted to access) applied to a Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance.
google_redis_cluster: `google_redis_cluster` provisions a Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance, a horizontally scalable, clustered deployment of managed Redis.
google_redis_instance: `google_redis_instance` provisions a Memorystore for Redis instance, a single-node or standard-tier managed Redis deployment.
google_redis_v1beta1_acl_policy: `google_redis_v1beta1_acl_policy` defines Redis ACL rule(s) (which command(s) and key pattern(s) a user is permitted to access) applied to a Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance.
google_redis_v1beta1_cluster: `google_redis_v1beta1_cluster` provisions a Memorystore for Redis Cluster instance, a horizontally scalable, clustered deployment of managed Redis.
google_redis_v1beta1_instance: `google_redis_v1beta1_instance` provisions a Memorystore for Redis instance, a single-node or standard-tier managed Redis deployment.
google_run_instance: `google_run_instance` is a single running container instance backing a Cloud Run service or job, the unit that actually executes request or task handling.
google_run_job: `google_run_job` runs a Cloud Run container to completion for a batch or scheduled task, rather than serving ongoing request traffic like a Cloud Run service.
google_run_service: `google_run_service` is a Cloud Run service, a deployed, autoscaling container that serves HTTP request traffic.
google_run_worker_pool: `google_run_worker_pool` runs a Cloud Run container that continuously processes work (e.g. from a queue) rather than serving inbound HTTP requests or running to completion like a job.
google_saasservicemgmt_release: `google_saasservicemgmt_release` is an App Lifecycle Manager (formerly SaaS Runtime) release, a real, versioned bundle of changes to a SaaS offering that gets deployed to `google_saasservicemgmt_unit`s via a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout`.
google_saasservicemgmt_rollout: `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` is the real process App Lifecycle Manager uses to update a SaaS offering's provisioned units with a new `google_saasservicemgmt_release`, following the sequencing and pacing strategy defined by its own `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout_kind`.
google_saasservicemgmt_rollout_kind: `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout_kind` defines the real rollout strategy (sequencing, batching, pacing) a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` follows when updating a SaaS offering's units in App Lifecycle Manager.
google_saasservicemgmt_saa: `google_saasservicemgmt_saa` represents a real SaaS offering (an "SaaS Application") registered in App Lifecycle Manager, the top-level resource whose `google_saasservicemgmt_unit`s get modeled, deployed, and operated through the service.
google_saasservicemgmt_tenant: `google_saasservicemgmt_tenant` is a real tenant of a SaaS offering managed through App Lifecycle Manager, the customer-facing boundary that rollouts and unit updates can be targeted at or excluded from.
google_saasservicemgmt_unit: `google_saasservicemgmt_unit` is App Lifecycle Manager's real term for one provisioned instance of a SaaS offering's deployed application or infrastructure, the thing a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` actually updates.
google_saasservicemgmt_unit_kind: `google_saasservicemgmt_unit_kind` classifies a `google_saasservicemgmt_unit` in App Lifecycle Manager, the real category a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` targets (optionally with additional filters) when deciding which units to update.
google_saasservicemgmt_unit_operation: `google_saasservicemgmt_unit_operation` is a real, tracked operation performed against a `google_saasservicemgmt_unit` in App Lifecycle Manager, such as a provisioning or update step carried out as part of a rollout.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag` is a real feature flag definition within a SaaS Service Management flag_set -- its own key, flag_value_type, and evaluation_spec -- so a feature's on/off or variant state can be controlled centrally across every unit that references this flag.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_attr: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_attribute` defines a real, named attribute (its own key and value_type/attribute_value_type) that a flag's own evaluation_spec can target on, so flag evaluation can vary by a real, declared property of the requesting context rather than only a static on/off value.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_rele: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_release` is a real, point-in-time release bundling a set of flags' own revisions together (flag_revisions, flag_revisions_release, flag_sets_release) -- effective_flag_revisions records what was actually live -- so a coordinated set of flag changes can be released and audited as one unit instead of each flag changing independently.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_revi: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_flag_revision` is a specific, versioned revision of a real flag's own evaluation_spec -- a snapshot of what that flag evaluated to at this revision -- so a flag's own history can be inspected and, if needed, referenced by a real flag_release.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_release: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_release` is an App Lifecycle Manager (formerly SaaS Runtime) release, a real, versioned bundle of changes to a SaaS offering that gets deployed to `google_saasservicemgmt_unit`s via a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout`.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_rollout: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_rollout` is the real process App Lifecycle Manager uses to update a SaaS offering's provisioned units with a new `google_saasservicemgmt_release`, following the sequencing and pacing strategy defined by its own `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout_kind`.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_rollout_k: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_rollout_kind` defines the real rollout strategy (sequencing, batching, pacing) a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` follows when updating a SaaS offering's units in App Lifecycle Manager.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_saa: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_saa` represents a real SaaS offering (an "SaaS Application") registered in App Lifecycle Manager, the top-level resource whose `google_saasservicemgmt_unit`s get modeled, deployed, and operated through the service.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_saas_rele: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_saas_release` is a real release record for a SaaS Service Management-managed service, tracked by its own uid and labels, so a specific release can be referenced and audited as its own resource.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_tenant: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_tenant` is a real tenant of a SaaS offering managed through App Lifecycle Manager, the customer-facing boundary that rollouts and unit updates can be targeted at or excluded from.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit` is App Lifecycle Manager's real term for one provisioned instance of a SaaS offering's deployed application or infrastructure, the thing a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` actually updates.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_grou: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_group` is a real, named grouping of SaaS Service Management units, tracked by its own uid and labels, so a set of related units can be managed and operated on together rather than individually.

`google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_group_operation` is a real, tracked operation performed against a unit_group -- its own uid and labels record which operation this is -- so a long-running or bulk change applied to a unit group can be inspected and audited as its own resource rather than only observed indirectly through the group's own eventual state.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_kind: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_kind` classifies a `google_saasservicemgmt_unit` in App Lifecycle Manager, the real category a `google_saasservicemgmt_rollout` targets (optionally with additional filters) when deciding which units to update.
google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_oper: `google_saasservicemgmt_v1beta1_unit_operation` is a real, tracked operation performed against a `google_saasservicemgmt_unit` in App Lifecycle Manager, such as a provisioning or update step carried out as part of a rollout.
google_sasportal_deployment: `google_sasportal_deployment` is a real organizational grouping of CBRS devices in the Google SAS Portal (Spectrum Access System), identified by a unique user ID; a SAS organization can contain multiple deployments, each typically holding multiple `google_sasportal_device` entries.
google_sasportal_device: `google_sasportal_device` is a real Citizens Broadband Radio Service Device (CBSD) registered and managed through the Google SAS Portal, requiring installation by a Certified Professional Installer before it's authorized to transmit on CBRS spectrum.
google_sasportal_node: `google_sasportal_node` is an organizational node in the Google SAS Portal's real device hierarchy, used alongside deployments to structure how CBRS devices and access are managed at scale.
google_secretmanager_secret: `google_secretmanager_secret` is a named secret in Secret Manager, that version(s) holding its own actual sensitive value are created under.
google_secretmanager_v1beta1_secret: `google_secretmanager_v1beta1_secret` is a named secret in Secret Manager, that version(s) holding its own actual sensitive value are created under.
google_secretmanager_v1beta2_secret: `google_secretmanager_v1beta2_secret` is a named secret in Secret Manager, that version(s) holding its own actual sensitive value are created under.
google_securesourcemanager_branch_rule: `google_securesourcemanager_branch_rule` enforces protections (required reviews, status checks, restricted force-push) on branch(es) matching a pattern within a Secure Source Manager repository.
google_securesourcemanager_hook: `google_securesourcemanager_hook` configures a webhook that Secure Source Manager calls out to on repository events (pushes, pull request changes), integrating with external CI/CD or notification systems.
google_securesourcemanager_instance: `google_securesourcemanager_instance` is the top-level, privately hosted Secure Source Manager deployment that repository/repositories are created within, isolated to a single Google Cloud project and VPC.
google_securesourcemanager_issue: `google_securesourcemanager_issue` is a tracked issue within a Secure Source Manager repository, used for bug and task tracking alongside the source code itself.
google_securesourcemanager_issue_comment: `google_securesourcemanager_issue_comment` is a single comment posted on a Secure Source Manager issue.
google_securesourcemanager_pull_request: `google_securesourcemanager_pull_request` proposes merging one branch into another within a Secure Source Manager repository, the unit code review and CI checks are attached to before merge.
google_securesourcemanager_pull_request_: `google_securesourcemanager_pull_request_comment` is a single review comment posted on a Secure Source Manager pull request, either general or attached to a specific line of the diff.
google_securesourcemanager_repository: `google_securesourcemanager_repository` is a Git repository hosted within a Secure Source Manager instance, Google Cloud's own fully managed, private source code hosting service.
google_securitycenter_big_query_export: `google_securitycenter_big_query_export` continuously streams Security Command Center finding(s) into a BigQuery dataset for custom analysis, dashboards, or long-term retention.
google_securitycenter_custom_module: `google_securitycenter_custom_module` defines a caller-written detection rule Security Command Center's Security Health Analytics evaluates alongside its own built-in detectors.
google_securitycenter_mute_config: `google_securitycenter_mute_config` automatically mutes matching Security Command Center finding(s), suppressing them from active alerting while keeping them recorded.
google_securitycenter_notification_confi: `google_securitycenter_notification_config` streams matching Security Command Center finding(s) to a Pub/Sub topic in real time as they're created or updated.
google_securitycenter_source: `google_securitycenter_source` registers an external or custom detector as a finding source within Security Command Center, letting it publish its own finding(s) alongside Google's built-in detectors.
google_securitycenter_v1beta1_source: `google_securitycenter_v1beta1_source` registers an external or custom detector as a finding source within Security Command Center, letting it publish its own finding(s) alongside Google's built-in detectors.
google_securityposture_posture: `google_securityposture_posture` defines a versioned bundle of Organization Policy constraint(s) and Security Health Analytics module setting(s) that Security Posture management can deploy as a unit.
google_securityposture_posture_deploymen: `google_securityposture_posture_deployment` applies a specific Security Posture posture version to a target organization, folder, or project, activating its own bundled policy and detector configuration there.
google_securityposture_report: `google_securityposture_report` is a Security Command Center report of infrastructure-as-code resources that violate an organization's own defined security posture, generated by validating a Terraform plan or similar declarative configuration ahead of deployment rather than after the fact.
google_servicedirectory_endpoint: `google_servicedirectory_endpoint` registers a specific address (IP and port) a Service Directory service can be reached at.
google_servicedirectory_namespace: `google_servicedirectory_namespace` is a container grouping related service(s) together within Service Directory, Google Cloud's own managed service registry.
google_servicedirectory_service: `google_servicedirectory_service` registers a logical service within Service Directory, that endpoint(s) advertising where it's actually reachable are attached to.
google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_endpoint: `google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_endpoint` registers a specific address (IP and port) a Service Directory service can be reached at.
google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_namespac: `google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_namespace` is a container grouping related service(s) together within Service Directory, Google Cloud's own managed service registry.
google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_service: `google_servicedirectory_v1beta1_service` registers a logical service within Service Directory, that endpoint(s) advertising where it's actually reachable are attached to.
google_servicemanagement_config: `google_servicemanagement_config` is a specific, versioned configuration (a Google Service Configuration) for a managed API, defining its own methods, quota, and monitoring behavior.
google_servicemanagement_rollout: `google_servicemanagement_rollout` publishes a specific Service Management configuration version live, making it the active configuration serving traffic for a managed API.
google_servicemanagement_service: `google_servicemanagement_service` registers a managed API with Service Management/Service Infrastructure, the underlying system that Google's own and many third-party Google Cloud APIs (including Endpoints-managed APIs) run on.
google_siteverification_site_verificatio: `google_siteverification_site_verification_web_resource` records a verified website or domain, confirming that the owner controls it via one of Google Site Verification real methods (a hosted file, an HTML meta tag, Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, a DNS TXT record, or a DNS CNAME record). Verification unlocks access to other Google services (e.g. Search Console) that require confirmed site or domain ownership, and each resource can list additional owner accounts beyond the one that performed the original verification.
google_sourcerepo_repo: `google_sourcerepo_repo` is a Git repository hosted on Cloud Source Repositories, Google Cloud's original private Git hosting service.
google_spanner_backup: `google_spanner_backup` is a point-in-time backup of a Spanner database, restorable to a new database within the same instance.
google_spanner_backup_schedule: `google_spanner_backup_schedule` automates recurring Spanner database backups on a defined cadence, instead of requiring each backup to be triggered manually.
google_spanner_database: `google_spanner_database` is a Spanner database, the schema and data container created within a Spanner instance that queries and transactions run against.
google_spanner_instance: `google_spanner_instance` is the top-level Spanner resource that provisions compute capacity (nodes or processing units) database(s) run on, and defines the region(s) data is replicated across.
google_spanner_instance_config: `google_spanner_instance_config` defines the geographic replication topology (which region(s) hold a read-write or read-only replica) a Spanner instance is created with.
google_spanner_instance_partition: `google_spanner_instance_partition` reserves a dedicated slice of compute capacity within a Spanner instance for a specific database or set of databases, isolating its own performance from the rest of the instance.
google_spanner_session: `google_spanner_session` is a connection context Spanner client libraries create to execute reads, writes, and transactions against a database, pooled and reused across requests for efficiency.
google_speech_custom_class: `google_speech_custom_class` is a Cloud Speech-to-Text custom class, a real, reusable list of domain-specific terms (like product names) used to bias transcription toward correctly recognizing those terms when they appear in audio.
google_speech_phrase_set: `google_speech_phrase_set` is a Cloud Speech-to-Text phrase set, a real, reusable collection of phrases and boost values (which can embed `google_speech_custom_class` entries) that hints the recognition model toward expected words and phrases in an audio request.
google_speech_v1p1beta1_custom_class: `google_speech_v1p1beta1_custom_class` is a Cloud Speech-to-Text custom class, a real, reusable list of domain-specific terms (like product names) used to bias transcription toward correctly recognizing those terms when they appear in audio.
google_speech_v1p1beta1_phrase_set: `google_speech_v1p1beta1_phrase_set` is a Cloud Speech-to-Text phrase set, a real, reusable collection of phrases and boost values (which can embed `google_speech_custom_class` entries) that hints the recognition model toward expected words and phrases in an audio request.
google_sqladmin_backup_run: `google_sqladmin_backup_run` is a single completed or in-progress backup of a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_database: `google_sqladmin_database` is a single logical database within a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_instance: `google_sqladmin_instance` is a Cloud SQL instance -- a fully managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server database server.
google_sqladmin_ssl_cert: `google_sqladmin_ssl_cert` is a client SSL certificate issued for authenticating a connection to a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_user: `google_sqladmin_user` is a database user account on a Cloud SQL instance, used to authenticate connections to its own database(s).
google_sqladmin_v1beta4_backup_run: `google_sqladmin_v1beta4_backup_run` is a single completed or in-progress backup of a Cloud SQL instance.

google_sqladmin_v1beta4_ssl_cert: `google_sqladmin_v1beta4_ssl_cert` is a client SSL certificate issued for authenticating a connection to a Cloud SQL instance.
google_sqladmin_v1beta4_user: `google_sqladmin_v1beta4_user` is a database user account on a Cloud SQL instance, used to authenticate connections to its own database(s).
google_storage_anywhere_cach: `google_storage_anywhere_cach` (Anywhere Cache) is a zonal, SSD-backed read cache for a Cloud Storage bucket, recently renamed Rapid Cache as part of the Cloud Storage Rapid family announced at Google Cloud Next '26 -- accelerating reads for AI training and analytics workloads without changing application code.
google_storage_bucket: `google_storage_bucket` is a Cloud Storage bucket, the top-level container that object(s) are uploaded into, with its own region, storage class, and access-control configuration.
google_storage_bucket_access_control: `google_storage_bucket_access_control` grants a specific access role (e.g. reader or owner) to an entity (a user, group, or `allUsers`) on an entire Cloud Storage bucket, via bucket-level ACLs.
google_storage_default_object_access_con: `google_storage_default_object_access_control` defines the ACL entry newly uploaded objects in a Cloud Storage bucket inherit by default, when the bucket uses fine-grained (rather than uniform) access control.
google_storage_folder: `google_storage_folder` is a real, hierarchical folder within a Cloud Storage bucket that has hierarchical namespace enabled, distinct from the flat, prefix-simulated "folders" of a standard bucket.
google_storage_hmac_key: `google_storage_hmac_key` is an HMAC credential pair for a Cloud Storage service account, used to authenticate requests through Cloud Storage's own S3-compatible XML API.
google_storage_managed_folder: `google_storage_managed_folder` defines a folder-like path prefix within a Cloud Storage bucket that its own IAM policy can be scoped to, letting different teams manage access to different prefixes within the same bucket.
google_storage_notification: `google_storage_notification` configures a Cloud Storage bucket to publish a Pub/Sub message whenever a specified object event (create, delete, and similar) occurs.
google_storage_object: `google_storage_object` is a single object (a file, blob, or piece of binary data) stored inside a Cloud Storage bucket.
google_storage_object_access_control: `google_storage_object_access_control` grants a specific access role (e.g. reader or owner) to an entity on a single Cloud Storage object, via object-level ACLs.
google_storage_rapid_cach: `google_storage_rapid_cach` (Rapid Cache, formerly Anywhere Cache) is a zonal, SSD-backed read cache for a Cloud Storage bucket, part of the Cloud Storage Rapid family announced at Google Cloud Next '26 -- accelerating reads for AI training, inference, and analytics workloads without requiring application code changes.
google_storagebatchoperations_job: `google_storagebatchoperations_job` runs a single bulk metadata or storage-class change operation across many Cloud Storage objects at once, rather than making individual per-object API calls.
google_storagetransfer_agent_pool: `google_storagetransfer_agent_pool` groups Storage Transfer Service agent(s) together, used when transferring data from an on-premises or non-cloud source that needs a local agent to read from.
google_storagetransfer_transfer_job: `google_storagetransfer_transfer_job` schedules a Storage Transfer Service job copying data between a source (another cloud, an on-premises system, or a Cloud Storage bucket) and a Cloud Storage destination.
google_testing_device_session: `google_testing_device_session` is a real Firebase Test Lab device session, an interactive connection to a physical or virtual test device used for exploratory, hands-on testing rather than an automated instrumentation or Robo test run.
google_testing_test_matrice: `google_testing_test_matrice` is a Firebase Test Lab test matrix, a real test run executed against every combination of the device dimensions (model, OS version, locale, orientation) specified for it, covering instrumentation, Robo, and Game Loop test types alike.
google_toolresults_execution: `google_toolresults_execution` is a Tool Results API execution, one real run of a test (for example one Firebase Test Lab test matrix run) within a `google_toolresults_history`, made up of one or more `google_toolresults_step` entries.
google_toolresults_history: `google_toolresults_history` is a Tool Results API history, the top-level container grouping every `google_toolresults_execution` that belongs to the same logical test target (such as one app) over time.
google_toolresults_perf_sample_sery: `google_toolresults_perf_sample_sery` is a Tool Results API performance sample series, a real, timestamp-ordered stream of performance samples (such as CPU, memory, or graphics metrics) captured during one `google_toolresults_step`, up to 5,000 samples per series.
google_toolresults_step: `google_toolresults_step` is a single real operation performed as part of a `google_toolresults_execution`, such as one test runner run or one compilation step, the unit performance sample series and results actually attach to.
google_tpu_node: `google_tpu_node` is a real, provisioned Cloud TPU node, the accelerator instance ML training and inference workloads run on, created directly or allocated through a `google_tpu_queued_resource` request.
